documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66 y/o man transferring care. Former PCP retired; he wants one doctor he can actually reach.

HPI: Here mostly to get his prescriptions under one roof. Long history of high blood pressure, on three agents for years. Coronary disease known to an outside cardiology group, who he sees about once a year; gets chest tightness only with heavy exertion (carrying groceries up the stairs fast, shoveling) maybe once every month or two, settles with rest, has used a nitro tablet a handful of times this year. No rest pain, no pain lasting more than a few minutes. No dyspnea, no orthopnea, no ankle swelling. Admits he doesn't always remember the evening routine but takes everything once a day in the morning.

PMH: hypertension; coronary artery disease with chronic stable angina (details with cardiology, records requested).
PSH: appendectomy at about 25.
Meds: lisinopril 10 daily, HCTZ 25 daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, ASA 81, atorvastatin 40, NTG 0.4 SL prn.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father had an MI at 64. Mother had high blood pressure and a stroke. One brother with type 2 diabetes.
SH: drove long-haul for decades, now retired. Lives alone; one daughter. Still smoking close to a pack a day, roughly 40 pack-years total. 2-3 beers most nights. Cooks for himself, lots of deli meat, frozen dinners, canned soup.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: BP elevated today (see vitals), recheck similar. Obese. Well-appearing. No JVD. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, healed RLQ scar. No edema, pedal pulses 2+.

Screens: PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 5 -- discussed cutting back, he is not interested in a change right now.

A/P:
1. HTN -- above goal today. He reports missed evening habits but the meds are all daily; continue current regimen, home cuff readings please, nurse BP check with flu shot next month.
2. CAD / stable angina -- stable pattern. Continue ASA, statin, beta blocker, NTG prn. Lipids today. Records from cardiology.
3. Tobacco -- 40 pk-yr, smoking now. Strongly advised quitting; declines patches or medication for now, "I'll do it my own way." Eligible for annual low-dose CT; ordered.
4. Health maintenance -- CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c (brother diabetic), one-time hep C and HIV screens. PCV20 and Tdap given today. Colonoscopy per old records, requesting.

RTC about 3 months.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: PCV20 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, Tdap 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated, observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Sheehan, your blood work is back. Kidney function, liver tests, blood counts and sugar (A1c) all look fine, and the hep C and HIV screens are negative. Your LDL (bad cholesterol) is in the 140s on the atorvastatin, which is higher than we'd want for someone with heart disease. Taking it every day matters, and cutting down on processed meats will help. We'll go over it at your next visit.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline)
Indication: 66-year-old current smoker, 40 pack-years.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Central airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.

conditions.label: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 78. Normal axis. Normal intervals. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No acute ST-segment changes.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy.

reports.text:
TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAM
Indication: dyspnea, hypertension.
Left ventricle: normal cavity size, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Normal wall motion. LVEF 55-60% (visual estimate). Mitral inflow and tissue Doppler show an impaired relaxation pattern.
Right ventricle: normal size and function.
Valves: no significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Preserved LV systolic function, LVEF 55-60%. Concentric LVH with impaired relaxation. Normal RV. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary -- Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 2025-02-05, discharged 2025-02-07.

Principal diagnosis: acute hypertensive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure), preserved ejection fraction.

History: 69-year-old man with hypertension, coronary artery disease with chronic stable angina and obesity, admitted with exertional breathlessness progressing over several months and occasional episodes of waking short of breath at night. He acknowledged taking his antihypertensives irregularly. Hydrochlorothiazide is his main stated BP drug.

On arrival: BP 160/90, HR 78, BMI 32. Presystolic (S4) gallop at the apex, accentuated in the left lateral decubitus position. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, creatinine 1.1, fasting glucose 98. Total cholesterol 210, LDL 140, HDL 40.
ECG: sinus rhythm, left ventricular hypertrophy.
Echo 2/6: LVEF 55-60%, concentric LVH, impaired relaxation, normal RV, no significant valvular disease.

Hospital course: Monitored on telemetry without arrhythmia. Home antihypertensives given daily under observation with improvement in BP and in breathing on ward ambulation. Extensive teaching on taking medications every day, sodium restriction and daily weights.

Discharge medications (unchanged): lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL prn chest pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit about a year ago; 2-3 beers nightly; retired long-haul truck driver; lives alone.
Family: father MI at 64; mother hypertension and stroke; brother type 2 diabetes.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; cardiology clinic in 6 weeks.

Hospital medicine / cardiology

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after receiving discharge summary. Home since Friday, says breathing 'much better.' Has all six meds at home, no changes made at discharge. Reviewed: take them every morning, use a pill box, weigh daily before breakfast, call for gain of 3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week or worse breathing. No bathroom scale -- will buy one. TCM visit booked 2/13.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 6 days after discharge (admitted 2/5-2/7, cardiology service, acute hypertensive HF with preserved EF). Discharge summary and echo reviewed.

He is breathing better. Walks to the mailbox and around the block without stopping. Sleeps flat, no waking up short of breath since he got home. No chest pain. Bought a scale, weights steady over 3 days. Admits that before the admission he went days at a time without his pills -- 'I'd take them when I remembered.' Now using a weekly pill organizer his daughter set up.

Meds reconciled: no changes at discharge. Lisinopril 10, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ 50, ASA 81, atorvastatin 40, NTG prn.

Exam: BP lower than hospital, still above goal. No JVD. Heart regular, S4 not appreciated today. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Heart failure with preserved EF, hypertensive heart disease -- added to problem list. Euvolemic. Daily weights, 2 g sodium, limit beer (also fluid). Call parameters reviewed.
2. HTN -- adherence was the main issue; continue regimen, recheck.
3. CAD -- no angina.
BMP today. Cardiology clinic 6 wks. RTC 3 months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium are normal. Keep up the daily weights and the pill box.

Outside cardiology group -- clinic visit 2025-03-19, post-hospital follow-up.

Dear colleague,
We saw Mr. Sheehan six weeks after his admission for hypertensive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF 55-60%, concentric LVH). His exertional breathlessness has improved and he has had no further nocturnal episodes. He is taking his medications daily with a pill organizer.

BP 142/86, HR 70. Lungs clear, no peripheral edema, no JVD.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, SL nitroglycerin prn. NKDA.

Impression: HFpEF due to hypertensive heart disease, clinically improved; stable angina, quiet. No medication changes today. Continue sodium restriction and daily weights.
Return in 6 months.

Cardiology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department -- visit 2026-02-08. Received by fax.

CC: shortness of breath, getting worse over about a week.

HPI: 70-year-old man with hypertension, coronary disease with stable angina, obesity and heart failure (hospitalized for it about a year ago), accompanied by his daughter. Breathing has worsened gradually through the week; he is more fatigued and some nights has slept sitting up in his recliner. Eating less. Denies chest pain, cough, fever or recent illness. Has not seen a doctor in several months. Lives alone.

Meds (per patient/daughter): lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: appendectomy.
FH: father MI at 64; mother HTN, stroke; brother T2DM.

Exam: Tired-appearing, mildly dyspneic, talking in short phrases. Heart regular rate and rhythm, apical impulse displaced laterally. Breath sounds decreased at both bases with crackles. No wheezes. No lower extremity edema. No JVD.

Results: NT-proBNP 2850 pg/mL. hs-troponin I 9 ng/L. BMP and CBC unremarkable.
CXR: enlarged heart, increased pulmonary vascular markings, subtle perihilar haziness.

ED course: furosemide 40 mg IV given with some improvement in work of breathing.

Impression: acute decompensated heart failure.
Disposition: admitted to hospital medicine.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, hospital medicine. Admitted 2026-02-08 via the ED, discharged 2026-02-11.

Diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure; underlying heart failure with preserved ejection fraction from hypertensive heart disease (echo 2/2025 LVEF 55-60%).
Other: hypertension, coronary artery disease with stable angina, obesity.

Course: Presented with a week of progressive dyspnea and orthopnea. NT-proBNP 2850, troponin not elevated, chest film with vascular congestion. Treated with IV furosemide with good diuresis; breathing returned to baseline and he was walking the hall on room air by day 3. Renal function and potassium stable through diuresis.

Discharge medications:
- NEW: furosemide 20 mg by mouth daily
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: daily weights, low-salt diet, take medications every day.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week (patient to call); cardiology clinic in 2-4 weeks.

Hospital Medicine
